threads.title: Seed keepers on two shores
threads.text: Three organisations keep living seed in circulation. Irish Seed Savers, near Lough Derg in East Clare, holds Ireland’s heritage seeds, grains and apple trees. In the Los Angeles basin, the Seed Library of Los Angeles helps residents grow and save open-pollinated seed, and the Theodore Payne Foundation offers seed from more than 200 California native species.
threads.how: Noticed by the River: each lists seed saving as its core work in its public profile. Irish Seed Savers is close to Corra Woods; the LA pair share one basin.
sources: The Clare Echo on 30 years of Irish Seed Savers

threads.title: Carers of the Los Angeles watershed
threads.text: TreePeople is based in Coldwater Canyon Park on Mulholland Drive in the Santa Monica Mountains, a short walk along the ridge from Laurel Canyon, and serves as Watershed Coordinator for the Santa Clara River Watershed. Friends of the Los Angeles River has led the Great LA River CleanUp for over 35 years, with the Los Angeles Conservation Corps and the Conservation Corps of Long Beach among its partners.
threads.how: Noticed by the River: both organisations publicly describe their work as caring for water across the LA basin. The FoLAR and Conservation Corps partnership is documented.
orgs: Friends of the Los Angeles River
sources: PBS SoCal: It takes a village to clean the L.A. River
NBC Los Angeles: 36th Great LA River Cleanup

threads.title: Land returning to the Tongva
threads.text: In 2022 the Tongva Taraxat Paxaavxa Conservancy, a Tongva-led nonprofit, received a one-acre site in Altadena, Huhuunga: the first land returned to the Tongva in Los Angeles County in nearly two centuries. Resource Generation Los Angeles and the Native American Land Conservancy supported the effort.
threads.how: Documented in the Conservancy’s own public statements and in reporting. Shared here as public history, with the Conservancy’s own site as the first source. The River follows their lead on anything more.
sources: Tongva Taraxat Paxaavxa Conservancy: purpose and vision
First Nations Development Institute: returning the people’s land
LAist: why a property worth millions was returned to the Tongva

threads.title: One network beneath Clare and Tipperary
threads.text: Irish Seed Savers in Scarriff is a member of the Irish Environmental Network. Across Lough Derg, Cloughjordan Ecovillage in County Tipperary, Ireland’s first ecovillage, receives annual funding through that same network for its education and advocacy work.
threads.how: Documented in public records of each organisation. The River noticed they share a network and a lake: Lough Derg lies between them.
sources: The Wheel: Cloughjordan Ecovillage case study

threads.title: A local ecovillage in a global web
threads.text: Cloughjordan Ecovillage is part of the Global Ecovillage Network, which links ecovillages and intentional communities around the world. Cloughjordan is home to Ireland’s first member-owned community supported agriculture farm.
threads.how: Documented by the ecovillage, the Global Ecovillage Network and reporting.
sources: The Irish Times: inside Ireland’s only ecovillage

threads.title: Farming with nature in the west of Clare
threads.text: The Burren Programme is a locally-led scheme in which farmers are paid for the health of the habitats they tend, and an independent evaluation found it strengthened ties among Burren farmers. Nearby in Ennistymon, Hometree restores native woodland and temperate rainforest in the west of Ireland.
threads.how: Noticed by the River: two west-of-Ireland efforts, both bringing farming and nature restoration together, in neighbouring parts of County Clare.
sources: gov.ie: Burren Programme payments and evaluation
EU CAP Network: evaluation of the Burren Programme

threads.title: Places that teach by doing
threads.text: Some places share what they learn openly. Cloughjordan Ecovillage shares its learning about low-carbon living through educational activities. The Burren Programme’s results are published in a public evaluation, so other regions can learn from it.
threads.how: Noticed by the River: both publish what they have learned for others to use.
sources: Transnational Institute: the future is now at Cloughjordan
EU CAP Network: evaluation of the Burren Programme

threads.title: Maps that talk to each other
threads.text: Murmurations is an open protocol that lets organisations publish their own profiles, which an index then gathers without owning them. Transition Towns and the EcoRestoration Alliance have worked on feeding their maps into it, and the CoBot search tool built on it now reaches over 80,000 organisations.
threads.how: Documented by the Murmurations and Open Co-op communities. Open data like this is where the River’s automatic threads will come from.

threads.title: Farms finding each other on Hylo
threads.text: Hylo created a Farm group type through an API integration with OpenTEAM, so farms and ranches can share profiles, products and their location on Hylo’s map. Hylo Projects also carry places and times, so work in progress appears on the map too.
threads.how: Documented in Hylo’s own release notes.
sources: Terran Collective: community infrastructure for regenerative agriculture

threads.title: Gatherings anyone can find
threads.text: Hylo’s public map and public events show gatherings from groups anywhere that choose to be open. Dandelion lists events from community-led organisers, the Institute of Relational Being among them. The Global Regeneration CoLab keeps an open community calendar of regenerative gatherings.
threads.how: Noticed by the River: two open places where gatherings are published. Only events their hosts mark as public appear.
sources: Institute of Relational Being on Dandelion

threads.title: Bioregional weavers, near and far
threads.text: The Global Regeneration CoLab offers peer-to-peer support to changemakers working on regenerative projects, and was started to meet the challenges of bioregional regeneration together. In Europe, the Bioregional Weaving Labs Collective, led by Ashoka and Commonland, has weaving labs in eight countries. One of these is in south-east Ireland, around County Waterford, and is now its own organisation. The Collective has also mapped more than 150 bioregional initiatives so people can find others working in their region.
threads.how: Documented on each network’s own pages. The River noticed they share one practice, weaving a region’s people and projects together, and that their calendars and maps are open to all.
orgs: Bioregional Weaving Lab South East Ireland
sources: Daniel Wahl: Accelerating bioregional regeneration and the GRC
GIY: about the Bioregional Weaving Labs Collective
GIY: Bioregional Weaving Lab South East Ireland

threads.title: Tending land after fire
threads.text: When the Eaton fire burned Huhuunga in January 2025, Tongva leaders said traditional land-tending practices had lessened the damage. TreePeople keeps a Wildfire Resilience Fund for Los Angeles’ hills and neighbourhoods.
threads.how: Noticed by the River: two responses to fire in the same mountains, shared gently, from public reporting and the organisations’ own pages.
sources: Wikipedia: Tongva Taraxat Paxaavxa Conservancy (citing the Los Angeles Times, January 2025)
